bullets.title: NVDA secures 35-40% of global HBM supply; UBS projects $1B/day FCF
bullets.body: Nvidia has locked up 35-40% of global HBM supply for next year and plans to ship 24-30GW of rack-level compute globally, per fintwit analysis. UBS models $1B/day in free cash flow with revenue consensus ranging $630B-$681B and some analysts above $700B. Ark Invest (Cathie Wood) also purchased 97,970 NVDA shares in the session.

bullets.title: NVDA backs $105B OpenAI Ohio data center; OpenAI chip commitments worth ~$600B through 2030
bullets.body: Nvidia agreed to back up to $105B of OpenAI's Ohio data center project, which includes 8GW of planned computing capacity and targets 800MW online by 2028. OpenAI's NVIDIA purchase commitments through 2030 are projected to generate approximately $600B in revenue for NVDA. Separately, NVDA's residual-value support on the Ohio facility is being structured to unlock non-hyperscaler AI financing channels, with SEC guidance limiting sponsor liability.

bullets.title: NVDA Spectrum-X CPO switches enter mass production with TSMC, Foxconn, ASE as partners
bullets.body: Nvidia's Spectrum-X co-packaged optics (CPO) switches for scale-out deployments have entered mass production with TSMC, Foxconn, and ASE as Taiwan manufacturing partners. Data centers are migrating to CPO from pluggables for power efficiency: CPO consumes <5 pJ/bit vs. 20-25 pJ/bit for pluggables.

bullets.title: HBM demand nearly doubles to 12.5EB in 2028; Broadcom could surpass NVIDIA in demand
bullets.body: HBM demand is projected to grow from 6.5-7EB in 2027 to 12.5EB in 2028, per fintwit analysis citing Meritz Securities. Meritz forecasts Broadcom at 35-40bn Gb of HBM demand in 2028, potentially exceeding NVIDIA at 30bn Gb, with Google ramping to 20bn Gb and AMD at 10bn Gb.

bullets.title: Fabrinet (FN) Q4 FY2026 earnings: positive read-throughs for AI networking ecosystem
bullets.body: Fabrinet Q4 FY2026 results flagged as materially positive for AI networking, optical communications, and custom compute manufacturing. Q1 guidance: adjusted EPS $4.10-$4.25 (beat vs. $4.00 consensus), revenue $1.38B-$1.43B. Fintwit noted FN expected to address 1.6T volume timelines, component shortages, NPO/CPO/OCS volumes, and China ban customer impacts.

bullets.title: COHR begins 300mm SiC substrate sampling; inflection point beyond optical components
bullets.body: Coherent has begun customer sampling of 300mm high thermal conductivity silicon carbide substrates that improve heat spreading by up to 25% vs. current solutions while maintaining compatibility. Fintwit commentary flags COHR as moving beyond purely optical components into high-value thermal solutions. PhotonCap's portfolio showed COHR +40.9% since July 30 call.

bullets.title: LITE and AXTI: InP supply thesis plays up 36-59% since August 2 call
bullets.body: PhotonCap flagged a LITE/AXTI InP (indium phosphide) supply thesis on August 2, noting an unusually large prepayment deal between LITE and AXTI to secure long-term InP supply. LITE is up ~36% and AXTI ~59% since that call. AXTI surged from $37 to $95 in a few weeks, prompting plans for a thesis update post.

bullets.title: MLCC supply in 'severe' shortage; Samsung lead times double to 40 weeks
bullets.body: ComponentNews has classified server MLCCs as in a 'severe' shortage stage, with Samsung reaching ~40-week lead times for high-capacitance MLCCs per DigiKey shipment data, up from ~20 weeks earlier this year. Fintwit argues NAND/MLCC/InP supply bottlenecks are structural and do not resolve simply with price declines.

bullets.title: VIAV: Rosenblatt bullish on 1.6T opportunity; CPO test shipments beginning
bullets.body: Rosenblatt highlighted VIAV's solid recent earnings and described the 1.6T test market as only in the 2nd-3rd inning. 1.6T test ASPs are roughly 50% higher than 800G, and CPO test shipments are beginning. Fintwit also flagged test as a major bottleneck in photonics broadly.

bullets.title: Nebius/Bloom Energy Vineland Planning Board approves AI campus 9-1
bullets.body: The Vineland, NJ Planning Board approved Nebius's AI infrastructure campus with a 9-1 vote, removing key local land-use risk for the NBIS/BE project. Nebius and Bloom announced 328 MW of installed capacity planned operational in 2026, though Nebius separately stated Vineland may not be operational until 2027.

bullets.title: Inventory build supports near-term component demand but creates future destocking risk for FN, COHR, LITE, MRVL, AVGO
bullets.body: Fintwit flagged that current inventory building is supporting near-term component demand but poses a tail risk of future destocking for optical/networking component suppliers. Communications infrastructure growth beyond AI data center reclassification is characterized as moderate-to-high positive for NOK, CSCO, CIEN, and FN.

bullets.title: China optical ban logic questioned: if packagers banned, who buys US high-end lasers?
bullets.body: Fintwit challenged the market's rally in optical names on China ban news, noting US firms supply high-end 200G EMLs to Chinese module makers who handle low-margin packaging—banning those packagers eliminates the demand for US laser suppliers. Lumentum and Coherent popped despite questionable fundamental logic, per the analysis.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Pixel manufacturing exits China by 2027; acquires Spirit Airlines data for AI training
bullets.body: Google has told suppliers it plans to move all Pixel smartphone, watch, and earbud production outside China starting next year. Separately, Google is acquiring Spirit Airlines' business data (emails, calendars, chats, documents) for ~$10M for AI training purposes. Alphabet also launched its first A$5B Australian-dollar bond sale to fund up to $205B in 2026 AI capex, and TPUv9 is rumored to maintain dual inference/training tracks.

bullets.title: INTC CEO buys $10M in INTC stock—largest insider purchase in company history
bullets.body: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan purchased $10 million of INTC stock, described by fintwit as the largest insider buy in Intel history, signaling strong management conviction.

bullets.title: TSLA Cybercab imminent Austin launch; Druckenmiller boosted AMZN and semiconductor exposure
bullets.body: Tesla has told staff it is gearing up for a public Cybercab launch this month in Austin—the first vehicle without a steering wheel or brake pedal. Separately, Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office significantly increased AMZN holdings in Q2 and boosted semiconductor positions ahead of the July market decline.

bullets.title: Anthropic ARR hits $65B; IPO expected within 2 months at ~$2T valuation
bullets.body: Anthropic's revenue run rate surpassed $65B ahead of its expected IPO within 2 months, with Polymarket pegging 44% odds it becomes the largest 2026 IPO. Fintwit models project $300-400B ARR by Dec-2027 at 10-12% monthly growth rates, with one analyst tagging $366B at 11.4% MoM. Investors flag implications for AI infrastructure suppliers including NVDA, MU, SNDK, LITE.

bullets.title: 30-year Treasury yield hits 5.32%—highest since 2007; global long bonds rising in concert
bullets.body: The U.S. 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.321%, its highest since mid-2007, with Japan's 10-year JGB hitting a 30-year high at 2.95% and Germany's 10-year at 3.22%, highest since May 2011. Fintwit warns that rising global long bond yields 'in concert is not a great signal for equities' and that a 100bp move today carries the impact of 300bp in the 1990s given larger bond market size and duration extension.

bullets.title: Oil surges: Brent above $91, WTI near $85 on stalled Hormuz talks; diesel crack hits record $102
bullets.body: Brent settled near $90.87/bbl (+2.65%) and WTI at $84.50/bbl (+2.55%) as U.S.-Iran truce extension was rejected by Trump and Hormuz negotiations stalled, with Chinese shippers COSCO and CMES halting tanker transit. Diesel crack spreads hit a record $102/bbl for the first time, with fintwit warning of potential industrial economy disruption. Polymarket places 60% odds of an Oman-Iran Hormuz deal within 30 days.

bullets.title: META faces landmark trial with up to $1.4T in potential damages from 29 states
bullets.body: 29 states are seeking penalties against Meta and platform changes including restrictions on young users, removal of infinite scroll, and removal of recommendation systems. Meta faces a landmark U.S. trial alleging Facebook and Instagram were designed to encourage compulsive use among minors, with potential damages cited at up to $1.4 trillion.

bullets.title: Taiwan power semis plan 10-15% price hike by October; SMIC raising mature node prices 15-20%
bullets.body: Taiwan power semiconductor makers are planning a third round of 2024 price hikes of 10-15% on non-contracted chips by October, driven by AI demand and following Infineon's lead. SMIC is simultaneously hiking Q3 prices 15-20% YoY on key mature technologies as AI drives demand for legacy-node chips.
